title: Enterprise Process Library and Operational Blueprints
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the company-wide operational policies and standardized procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and common internal templates. It is intended as the single-source reference for teams implementing or auditing cross-functional workflows.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and contingent workers across global regions. Exceptions must be approved by the owning team and recorded in the policy exceptions tracker.

Principles

- Safety-first: Preserve customer and company data confidentiality and integrity by default.
- Least privilege: Access granted only for specific, timeboxed tasks.
- Clear ownership: Every process step must name an accountable role.
- Auditability: Actions and approvals must be traceable in company systems.
- Efficient operations: Balance control with predictable SLAs to avoid operational friction.

Governance and Owners

- Policy Owner: Finance & Legal (primary), Security (technical guidance), People Ops (people/process enforcement).
- Executive Sponsor: VP Operations.
- Operational Owners and Contacts:
  - Access & Permissions: Access Administration (access-admin@redwood.example.com)
  - Change Management: Platform Engineering (change-mgr@redwood.example.com)
  - Data Management: Data Stewardship (data-steward@redwood.example.com)
  - Procurement & Expenses: Procurement (procurement@redwood.example.com)
  - Vendor Management: Vendor Risk & Compliance (vendor-risk@redwood.example.com)
  - Travel & Expenses: People Ops (travel@redwood.example.com)

1) Access & Permissions

Summary: Use least privilege and time-limited approvals for systems. Primary identity provider is Okta; resource-specific access is governed via AWS IAM, GCP IAM, and internal RBAC in the Redwood Console.

Roles and Authority:
- Requestor: employee or manager who requests access.
- Approver: role owner (service owner) or delegated approver.
- Access Admin: implements changes in IAM/Okta and records audit entries.
- Privileged Access Reviewer: security team member for periodic reviews.

Standard request flows:
1. Standard (non-privileged) access: Raise request in Jira (project: ACCESS-REQ) or via self-service Confluence form. Manager approval required. SLA: implemented within 24 hours for routine requests.
2. Privileged access (production systems, secrets, or escalation tooling): Requestor must provide justification, duration, and rollback plan. Approval chain: manager -> service owner -> security (Privileged Access Board). SLA: 72 hours target for approvals; emergency access via break-glass flow (see Emergency Access Runbook link).
3. Temporary access: Requests may include expiry (default 7 days). Access Admin will configure automatic expiration where supported.

Access reviews and recertification:
- Quarterly privileged access review owned by Security.
- Semi-annual standard access recertification owned by managers; automated reminders issued via Okta.

Minimum technical controls:
- MFA enforced for all interactive accounts (Okta verify or hardware token).
- Password managers (company-approved) required for shared credentials; avoid manual sharing.
- Secrets stored in company KMS/HSM-backed vault (HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS).

2) Change Management

Purpose: Ensure controlled, auditable changes to production and customer-facing systems while minimizing outage risk.

Change categories:
- Standard Change: Pre-approved, documented repeatable change (e.g., scheduled config refresh). No CAB approval required if checklist met.
- Normal Change: Requires RFC in Jira (project: CHG-RFC), impact assessment, test plan, backout plan, and CAB approval if risk > low.
- Emergency Change: Urgent fixes to mitigate active incidents; must use Emergency Change workflow and be reviewed post-implementation.

Process Summary:
1. Create RFC in CHG-RFC with owner, roll-out window, test plan, backout plan, and stakeholders.
2. Review window: 48 hours for Normal Changes.
3. CAB: Weekly standing CAB for non-emergency approvals; security and SRE must attend for high-risk changes.
4. Implementation: follow deployment checklist; observe monitoring and alert windows.
5. Post-deploy verification & close RFC.

SLOs & thresholds:
- RFC triage: 24-48 hours.
- Emergency change post-mortem: within 72 hours of change.

Tooling & Audit:
- All RFCs logged in Jira (CHG-RFC) with owner and links to runbooks.
- Deployment metadata must include build SHA, model variant, runtime config, and canary percent where applicable.

3) Data Management

Classification:
- Public: Allowed for public distribution.
- Internal: Default for non-sensitive company information.
- Restricted: Customer data, contracts, and PII that require access controls.
- Confidential: Legal, M&A, or regulated data with strict handling and retention.

Handling rules by class:
- Public: No special controls.
- Internal: Store in company-managed drives; standard backups.
- Restricted: Encrypt at-rest and in-transit, access via least privilege, logging enabled, DLP policies enforced.
- Confidential: Access on approved devices only, dual approval for exports, mandatory legal review for sharing outside company.

Retention & deletion:
- Audit logs: 1 year (full retention); aggregated metrics kept 3 years.
- Financial/contract records: 7 years per finance policy.
- Customer datasets used for evaluation: retention limited to project duration + 90 days unless contract states otherwise.

Data movement & third parties:
- Data exports to vendors require vendor classification and approved data processing agreement (DPA).
- Encrypted transfer only (TLS 1.2+). Use secure SFTP or signed API endpoints.

Data incidents:
- Any suspected data leak reported to Security in 1 hour.
- Incident response runbook invoked; notifications per Legal/Compliance templates.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- Purchase < $5,000: Department Manager approval. Target processing SLA: 48 business hours.
- $5,000 - $50,000: Director approval + Procurement review. SLA: 5 business days for standard vendor contracts.
- > $50,000 or multi-year commitments: VP approval + Legal sign-off + Procurement lead. SLA: 10-21 business days depending on negotiation complexity.

Contracting & legal review:
- All vendor contracts with data handling, indemnity, or IP clauses must be routed to Legal.
- Standard purchasing templates (NetSuite PO, SOW template) are required for commitments > $25k.

Expense policy highlights:
- Employees must submit expense reports within 7 days of trip completion.
- Receipts required for items > $25.
- Corporate card allowed for travel and vendor meals only; personal reimbursements require manager approval.

Vendor payments and fiscal controls:
- Vendor onboarding into AP requires completed W-9 (US) or equivalent tax form, banking details verified, and PO or approved contract attached.
- Invoice payment terms default to Net 30 unless negotiated.

5) Vendor Management and Risk Assessment

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
1. Vendor intake form in Confluence/Procurement portal.
2. Business justification and owner.
3. Security questionnaire if vendor processes Restricted/Confidential data.
4. DPA and liability review by Legal.
5. Insurance and SOC 2/ISO evidence where applicable.
6. Approved by Procurement and Legal.

Risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (High risk): Vendors processing customer data or offering critical infrastructure. Controls: annual penetration test evidence, SOC2 Type II, formal SLA, and quarterly performance reviews.
- Tier 2 (Moderate): Vendors with internal access or moderate data. Controls: security questionnaire, semi-annual review.
- Tier 3 (Low): Standard SaaS with no sensitive data. Controls: standard contract review and annual renewal check.

Offboarding:
- Revoke access within 24 hours of contract end.
- Retrieve company assets and credentials.
- Confirm data deletion per contract (evidence uploaded to vendor portal).

6) Travel Policy (high level)

Booking and approvals:
- All international travel requires trip request submitted to People Ops with manager approval at least 14 days in advance.
- Domestic travel: manager approval suggested 7 days in advance.

Preferred vendors and class of service:
- Economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business for flights over 6 hours or for VP+ roles with pre-approved exceptions.
- Use company-approved hotels and negotiated rates where available.

Per diem and reimbursements:
- Meals: per diem $75/day domestic, $100/day international (adjusted per country where policy provides).
- Incidentals require receipts for reimbursement.

Expense submission and audit:
- Submit receipts and expense report within 7 days of trip completion.
- People Ops audits 10% of travel reports quarterly for policy compliance.

Safety & security:
- Employees traveling to high-risk geographies must enroll in the company travel safety program and notify People Ops.

7) Internal Templates and Quick References

Included templates (links to Confluence templates):
- Access Request Template (ACCESS-REQ form)
- RFC Template (CHG-RFC) with rollout and roll-back checklist
- Vendor Intake Form and Security Questionnaire
- Standard Procurement SOW and PO Checklist
- Expense Report Template and Corporate Card Usage Guide
- Incident Notification Templates for Data and Security events

How to use templates: Create a copy of the canonical template page, fill required fields, attach artifacts (test results, screenshots), and link the artifact in the Jira ticket.

8) Exceptions, Waivers, and Continuous Improvement

- Exceptions: Must be requested via the policy exceptions tracker and include mitigation plans, owner, and expiration date. Executive approval required for exceptions > 90 days.
- Periodic review: This document will be reviewed annually by Finance & Legal with input from Security and People Ops.
- Continuous improvement: Teams should file process improvement requests in the OPERATIONS-IMPR Jira board.

B. Quick SLAs summary:
- Standard access requests: 24 hours
- Privileged access requests: 72 hours (target)
- RFC triage: 24-48 hours
- Procurement < $5k: 48 business hours
- Vendor onboarding (Tier 1): 10 business days typical
